candidates.changed_node: outer MULT: CS_RANK(TS_MEAN($dollar_volume,21)) scaling a new close-vs-21d-low bounce ratio
candidates.rationale: A contributes its whole 3-node liquidity level, TS_MEAN($dollar_volume,21). B contributes its rolling-low anchor TS_MIN($low,21) (3 nodes), rebuilt as a bounce-off-low ratio ($close over that anchor, minus 1) rather than B's own min-max stochastic, so no larger fragment of B is reused. Fusion: cross-sectional liquidity rank gates the bounce signal -- a rebound off the 21-day low counts for more in high-dollar-volume names where the reversal is actually tradeable, and is discounted in thin names where an apparent bounce is more likely microstructure noise. Neither parent alone has this: A carries no price-location information, and the bounce ratio alone has no liquidity context.

candidates.changed_node: RANK($roa) multiplying a fresh TS_MAX($high,21)-minus-close drawdown, vol-normalized
candidates.rationale: B, RANK($roa), is only 2 nodes total, so no child can ever share a 3-node fragment with it; it is kept whole (2 nodes, the maximum overlap achievable). A contributes TS_MAX($high,21) (3 nodes), rebuilt as a fresh vol-normalized drawdown-from-high rather than A's own min-max stochastic. Fusion: quality gates a pullback-timing signal -- a drawdown is worth buying only in fundamentally strong names, since pure price reversion (A) can't distinguish a discounted quality name from a deteriorating one, and a bare quality rank (B) carries no timing information at all.

candidates.changed_node: RANK($roa) divided by a fresh close-normalized 21d range-volatility average built from B's ($high-$low) core
candidates.rationale: A, RANK($roa), is only 2 nodes total and cannot supply a literal 3-node fragment; it is kept whole as the maximum possible overlap. B contributes its ($high-$low) range core (3 nodes), renormalized by $close instead of B's own $open and over a shorter window (21 vs 63), so B's own 7-node ratio is not reproduced. Fusion: quality-per-unit-of-risk -- dividing profitability rank by realized range-volatility isolates 'safe quality' (profitable and low-vol), which neither a bare quality rank (blind to risk) nor a volatility ratio (blind to fundamentals) captures alone.

candidates.changed_node: SUB of two CS_RANKs: same-day range/liquidity rank minus same-day range/price rank
candidates.rationale: A and B are close siblings -- both are TS_MEAN(($high-$low)/(X+eps),N), differing only in X (open vs dollar_volume) and window -- so a raw ratio of the two full averages would algebraically collapse toward a plain volume measure and add little; flagging that rather than forcing a trivial combination. Both share their ($high-$low) range core (3 nodes); the denominators are freshly smoothed over a new window (5, not 63/10) so neither parent's own 7-node ratio is reproduced. The genuine fusion is a rank-space divergence, not a ratio: CS_RANK(range/liquidity) minus CS_RANK(range/price) is positive when a stock's range looks large for its trading activity even after controlling for its ordinary price-normalized volatility -- an illiquidity-stress signal that volatility alone doesn't explain.

candidates.changed_node: MULT: B's TS_DECAY_LINEAR(-$return,3) scaling A's ($high-$low) over a fresh TS_RANK($dollar_volume,21)
candidates.rationale: B's only complete fragments are 2 nodes (-$return, or CS_ZSCORE($operating_margin)) or the whole 7-node call -- no exact 3-node piece exists -- so its smallest sub-expression of at least 3 nodes, TS_DECAY_LINEAR(-$return,3) (4 nodes), is used as the minimal faithful inheritance available. A's ($high-$low) core (3 nodes) is paired with a fresh TS_RANK($dollar_volume,21) denominator rather than A's own dollar-volume-average ratio. Fusion: the decay-weighted reversal is amplified on days whose range is large relative to how thin recent trading has been (low dollar-volume percentile) -- thin trading exaggerates ranges, and the resulting move is more likely a liquidity-driven overreaction that reverts, which neither A's static liquidity-range ratio nor B's plain reversal captures alone.

candidates.changed_node: MULT: A's TS_DECAY_LINEAR(-$return,3) scaling a fresh TS_MAX($high,21)-vs-close pullback ratio from B
candidates.rationale: A's only complete fragments are 2 or 4 nodes (same shape as pair 5's parent): TS_DECAY_LINEAR(-$return,3) (4 nodes) is its smallest available organ of at least 3, used here as the minimal faithful inheritance. B contributes TS_MAX($high,21) (3 nodes), rebuilt as a fresh close-vs-high pullback ratio rather than B's own min-max stochastic. Fusion: the short-term decay-weighted reversal is scaled up the further the stock sits below its 21-day high, and toward zero near the high -- a reversal after a real pullback is a stronger mean-reversion setup than one firing at new highs, an interaction neither A (no positional context) nor B (no return-timing) supplies alone.

candidates.changed_node: DIV: A's TS_MAX($high,21)-minus-close pullback discounted by a fresh range/dollar-volume illiquidity proxy from B
candidates.rationale: A contributes TS_MAX($high,21) (3 nodes) rebuilt as a distance-below-the-high pullback measure rather than A's own min-max stochastic. candidates.changed_node: RANK($roa) divided by a fresh smoothed-denominator illiquidity ratio built from B's ($high-$low) core
candidates.rationale: A, RANK($roa), is only 2 nodes total -- the same structural ceiling as pairs 2 and 3 -- so no child can share 3 nodes with it; it is kept whole as the maximum possible overlap. B contributes its ($high-$low) range core (3 nodes) with a freshly-smoothed denominator (window 5, not B's 10, and TS_MEAN-smoothed rather than the bare field) so B's own 7-node ratio is not reproduced. prompt:
You are proposing quantitative factor expressions for US large-cap equities.

Universe and data
- S&P 500 point-in-time constituents, roughly 500 names per day.
- Daily bars only, plus point-in-time quarterly fundamentals stamped from the
  report date. Every field is referenced with a leading `$`:
    $open $high $low $close $adj_close $volume $dollar_volume $return
    $roa $roe $operating_margin $leverage $asset_turnover
    $book_per_share $earnings_per_share $accrual_gap
  A bare name such as `close` is not a field and will be rejected.
- Execution convention: the signal is computed after the close of day T and the
  position is entered at the open of T+1.
- The window these factors are fitted and judged on runs from 2000 to 2013.
  Do not reason about anything later; you will never be shown a number from
  outside that window.

Syntax
- Operators are function calls: TS_MEAN, TS_STD, TS_MAX, TS_MIN, TS_RANK,
  TS_DELTA, TS_CORR, TS_COV, TS_SUM, TS_PRODUCT, TS_ARGMAX, TS_ARGMIN,
  TS_DECAY_LINEAR, EMA, DELAY, DELTA, RANK, ZSCORE, CS_RANK, CS_ZSCORE,
  CS_DEMEAN, IF, IF_ELSE, MIN, MAX, ABS, SIGN, LOG, LN, SQRT, POWER, BOUND,
  COUNT.
- Lookback windows must be positive integer literals, e.g. TS_MEAN($close, 21).
- Guard every division with a small epsilon: `/ (TS_STD($close, 21) + 1e-8)`.
- Well-formed example: -RANK(TS_CORR(RANK($close), RANK($volume), 5))

Hard limits every proposal must satisfy, or it is rejected before it is scored
- at most 200 characters
- at most 5 distinct `$fields`
- at most 4 free numeric constants (lookback windows and
  the 1e-8 epsilon guard do not count)
- expression tree depth at most 6
- must not share a complete sub-expression of 4 or more
  nodes with any published Alpha101 formula, or with any factor already in the
  archive. Restating a published alpha is the one thing that is always rejected.
- must cover at least 90% of the panel
- absolute rank correlation below 0.80 against every archive member

Output
- Return valid JSON only, matching the supplied JSON schema. No prose outside it.
